title.en: Volume 129 Biographies 54: Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, Yan
title.raw: 卷一百二十九 列傳第五十四 裴崔盧李王嚴 Volume 129 Biographies 54: Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, Yan

sentences.zh: 裴崔盧李王嚴

translations.literal: Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, Yan
translations.idiomatic: Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, and Yan

sentences.zh: ◎裴崔盧李王嚴

translations.literal: ◎ Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, Yan
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, and Yan

sentences.zh: 裴守真，絳州稷山人，後魏冀州刺史叔業六世孫。

translations.literal: Pei Shouzhen, a native of Jishan in Jiangzhou, was a sixth-generation descendant of Shu Ye, Governor of Ji in the Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shouzhen was a native of Jishan in Jiangzhou; he was a sixth-generation descendant of Shu Ye, Governor of Ji in the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父諲，隋大業中為淮安司戶參軍。

translations.literal: His father Yin, in the Daye period of Sui, served as Assistant Registrar of Huaian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin served as Assistant Registrar of Huaian in the Daye era of Sui.

sentences.zh: 郡人楊琳、田瓚等亂，劫吏多死，唯諲以仁愛故，賊約其屬無敢害，護送還鄉。

translations.literal: When Yang Lin, Tian Zan, and others of the commandery rebelled, most officials seized in the raid died; only Yin, because of his humane kindness, had the bandits instruct their followers not to harm him, and they escorted him back to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Lin, Tian Zan, and others of the commandery rebelled, most officials were killed in the raid; only Yin, because of his humane kindness, had the bandits instruct their followers not to harm him, and they escorted him back to his home village.

sentences.zh: 守真早孤，母喪，哀毀臒盡。

translations.literal: Shouzhen was orphaned early; when his mother died, his grief was so extreme that he wasted away to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was orphaned early; when his mother died, his grief was so extreme that he wasted away to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，六科連中，累調乾封尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, scored successively in six subjects, and was repeatedly promoted to the post of Magistrate of Qianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, scored successively in six subjects, and was repeatedly promoted to the post of Magistrate of Qianfeng.

sentences.zh: 養寡姊謹甚，士推其禮法。

translations.literal: He supported his widowed elder sister with the utmost care; scholars acclaimed him for his propriety and ritual conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He supported his widowed elder sister with the utmost care; scholars acclaimed him for his propriety and ritual conduct.

sentences.zh: 永淳初，關中旱，悉稟祿奉姊及諸甥，與妻息惡食不贍也。

translations.literal: In the early Yongchun period, when Guanzhong suffered drought, he allotted his entire salary to his sister and all his nephews and nieces, while he and his wife and children ate coarse food and could not feed themselves adequately.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongchun period, when Guanzhong suffered drought, he allotted his entire salary to his sister and all his nephews and nieces, while he and his wife and children ate coarse food and could not feed themselves adequately.

sentences.zh: 授太常博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Doctor of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Doctor of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 守真善容典，時謂才稱其官。

translations.literal: Shouzhen was skilled in ceremonial matters and musical standards; at the time people said his talent matched his office.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was skilled in ceremonial matters and musical standards, and at the time people said his talent matched his office.

sentences.zh: 高宗將封嵩山，詔諸儒議射牲事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong was about to perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Song, he ordered the Confucian scholars to discuss the matter of shooting the sacrificial victims.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong was about to perform the feng sacrifice on Mount Song, he ordered the Confucian scholars to discuss the matter of shooting the sacrificial victims.

sentences.zh: 守真奏：「古者郊祀天地，天子自射牲。

translations.literal: Shouzhen memorialized: "In antiquity, when sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars, the Son of Heaven shot the victims himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen memorialized: "In antiquity, when sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the suburban altars, the Son of Heaven shot the victims himself.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝封太山，令侍中儒者射之，帝不親也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Han enfeoffed Mount Tai, he had attendant gentlemen and Confucians shoot them; the Emperor did not do so in person.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Han enfeoffed Mount Tai, he had attendant gentlemen and Confucians shoot them; the Emperor did not do so in person.

sentences.zh: 今按禮，前明十五刻，宰人鸞刀割牲，質明行事，毛血已具，天子至，奠玉酌獻而已。

translations.literal: Now, according to the Rites, at the quarter-hour before dawn the butcher takes the luan knife and slaughters the victims; at daybreak the ceremony proceeds, and by then the hair and blood are already prepared. When the Son of Heaven arrives, he need only set down the jade and pour the libation.
translations.idiomatic: Now, according to the Rites, at the quarter-hour before dawn the butcher takes the luan knife and slaughters the victims; at daybreak the ceremony proceeds, and by then the hair and blood are already prepared. When the Son of Heaven arrives, he need only set down the jade and pour the libation.

sentences.zh: 今若前祀一日射牲，則早於事；

translations.literal: If one shoots the victims a day before the sacrifice, that is too early for the rite;
translations.idiomatic: If one shoots the victims a day before the sacrifice, that is too early for the rite;

sentences.zh: 及日，則晚不逮事。

translations.literal: if one does it on the day itself, it is too late and will not meet the requirements of the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: if one does it on the day itself, it is too late and will not meet the requirements of the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 漢又天子不親，古今異宜，恐不可行。

translations.literal: Under Han too the Son of Heaven did not shoot in person; ancient and modern practice differ, and I fear this cannot be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han too the Son of Heaven did not shoot in person; ancient and modern practice differ, and I fear this cannot be carried out.

sentences.zh: 」是時，《破陣》、《慶善》二樂舞入，帝常立以視，須樂闋乃坐。

translations.literal: " At that time the two dance pieces Po Zhen and Qing Shan were introduced; the Emperor would often stand to watch them and would not sit until the music ended.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the two dance pieces Po Zhen and Qing Shan were introduced; the Emperor would often stand to watch them and would not sit until the music ended.

sentences.zh: 守真並言：「二舞誠祖宗盛德，然古無天子立觀者。

translations.literal: Shouzhen also stated: "These two dances truly embody the great virtue of our ancestors, yet in antiquity there was no precedent for the Son of Heaven to stand and watch.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen also stated: "These two dances truly embody the great virtue of our ancestors, yet in antiquity there was no precedent for the Son of Heaven to stand and watch.

sentences.zh: 化育詒庇，孰非闕功，不應鼓舞別申嚴奉。

translations.literal: In nourishing and transforming all under Heaven and extending shelter to them, whose merit is not a matter of highest consequence? One should not, through drumming and dancing, set them apart for exceptional reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In nourishing and transforming all under Heaven and extending shelter to them, whose merit is not a matter of highest consequence? One should not, through drumming and dancing, set them apart for exceptional reverence.

sentences.zh: 」詔可，未及行。

translations.literal: " The edict approved [his views], but before they could be implemented—
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved his views, but before they could be implemented—

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，大行舊禮無在者，守真與博士韋叔夏、輔抱素等討按故事，稱情為文，鹹適所宜，時人服其得禮。

translations.literal: the Emperor died. There was no surviving precedent for the mourning rites of a Grand Procession. Shouzhen, together with the Doctors Wei Shuxia and Fu Baosu and others, searched out precedents, shaped sentiments into text, and all fitted what was appropriate; people at the time admired that they had grasped the rites.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor died. There was no surviving precedent for the mourning rites of a Grand Procession. Shouzhen, together with the Doctors Wei Shuxia and Fu Baosu and others, searched out precedents, shaped sentiments into text, and all fitted what was appropriate; people at the time admired that they had grasped the rites.

sentences.zh: 天授中，為司府丞，推核詔獄，多裁恕，全免數十姓。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou period he served as Assistant Director of the Department of Public Works; in investigating cases by imperial edict he often showed clemency in judgment and fully exonerated dozens of clans.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou period he served as Assistant Director of the Department of Public Works; in investigating cases by imperial edict he often showed clemency in judgment and fully exonerated dozens of clans.

sentences.zh: 不合武後旨，出為汴州司馬。

translations.literal: Because this did not accord with Empress Wu's intent, he was sent out as Assistant Administrator of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because this did not accord with Empress Wu's intent, he was sent out as Assistant Administrator of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷累成州刺史，政不務威嚴，吏民兩懷之。

translations.literal: After successive promotions he became Prefect of Chengzhou; in governing he did not rely on severity and awe, and both officials and commoners were attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: After successive promotions he became Prefect of Chengzhou; in governing he did not rely on severity and awe, and both officials and commoners were attached to him.

sentences.zh: 徙寧州，送者千數，出境尚不止。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to Ningzhou, more than a thousand people came to see him off; even after he had left the prefecture they would not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Ningzhou, more than a thousand people came to see him off; even after he had left the prefecture they would not turn back.

sentences.zh: 長安中卒，贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the Chang'an period and was posthumously given the office of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Chang'an period and was posthumously given the office of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 子子余、耀卿、巨卿。

translations.literal: His sons were Ziyu, Yaoqing, and Juqing.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ziyu, Yaoqing, and Juqing.

sentences.zh: 曾孫行立。

translations.literal: His great-grandson was Xingli.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson was Xingli.

sentences.zh: 耀卿、巨卿別有傳。

translations.literal: Yaoqing and Juqing have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoqing and Juqing have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 子余事繼母以孝聞，中明經，補鄠尉。

translations.literal: Ziyu was famed for filial piety toward his stepmother; he passed the mingjing examination and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of E.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu was famed for filial piety toward his stepmother; he passed the mingjing examination and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of E.

sentences.zh: 時同舍李朝隱、程行諶以文法稱，而子余以儒顯，或問優劣於長史陳崇業，答曰：「蘭菊異芬，胡有廢者？」

translations.literal: At the time his colleagues in the same lodging, Li Chaoyin and Cheng Xingchen, were celebrated for mastery of penal and administrative law, while Ziyu was distinguished for Confucian learning. When someone asked the Chief Commandant Chen Chongye which was superior, he answered: "Orchid and chrysanthemum have different fragrances—how could one discard either?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time his colleagues in the same lodging, Li Chaoyin and Cheng Xingchen, were celebrated for mastery of penal and administrative law, while Ziyu was distinguished for Confucian learning. When someone asked the Chief Commandant Chen Chongye which was superior, he answered: "Orchid and chrysanthemum have different fragrances—how could one discard either?"

sentences.zh: 景龍中，為左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong period he served as Investigating Censor of the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong period he served as Investigating Censor of the Left Office.

sentences.zh: 涇、岐有隋世番戶子孫數千家，司農卿趙履溫奏籍為奴婢，充賜口。

translations.literal: In Jing and Qi there were several thousand descendants of the Sui-era fan households. Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Zhao Lüwen memorialized to register them as slaves and servants to supply as gift recipients.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing and Qi there were several thousand descendants of the Sui-era fan households. Director of the Directorate of Agriculture Zhao Lüwen memorialized to register them as slaves and servants to supply as gift recipients.

sentences.zh: 子余曰：「官戶以恩原為番戶，且今又子孫，可抑為賤乎？

translations.literal: Ziyu said: "Official households were originally granted favor and reclassified as fan households; moreover they now have descendants—how can they be demoted to mean status?
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu said: "Official households were originally granted favor and reclassified as fan households; moreover they now have descendants—how can they be demoted to mean status?

sentences.zh: 」履溫倚宗楚客勢，辯於廷，子余執對不撓，遂詘其議。

translations.literal: " Lüwen relied on the power of Zong Chuke and was eloquent in court, but Ziyu held to his rebuttal without yielding, and in the end Lüwen's proposal was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: " Lüwen relied on the power of Zong Chuke and was eloquent in court, but Ziyu held to his rebuttal without yielding, and in the end Lüwen's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 開元初，累遷冀州刺史，為政惠裕，人稱有恩。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan period he was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Jizhou; in administration he was generous and lenient, and people praised him for his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan period he was repeatedly promoted to Prefect of Jizhou; in administration he was generous and lenient, and people praised him for his kindness.

sentences.zh: 入為岐王府長史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Chief Administrator of the Princedom of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Chief Administrator of the Princedom of Qi.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous title was Xiao (Filial).
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his posthumous title was Xiao (Filial).

sentences.zh: 時程行諶謚貞。

translations.literal: At the time Cheng Xingchen's posthumous title was Zhen (Upright).
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cheng Xingchen's posthumous title was Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 中書令張說嘆曰：「二謚可無愧矣！

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue exclaimed: "The two posthumous names are without shame!
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue exclaimed: "The two posthumous names are without shame!

sentences.zh: 」子余居官清，家闈友愛，兄弟六人，皆有誌行雲。

translations.literal: " Ziyu in office was upright; at home he was affectionate toward his family. Among six brothers, all had ambition and conduct worthy of note.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziyu in office was upright; at home he was affectionate toward his family. Among six brothers, all had ambition and conduct worthy of note.

sentences.zh: 行立，重然諾，學兵有法。

translations.literal: Xingli placed great weight on keeping his word and studied military methods with discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Xingli placed great weight on keeping his word and studied military methods with discipline.

sentences.zh: 母亡，泣血幾毀。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he wept blood and nearly destroyed himself [with grief].
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he wept blood and nearly destroyed himself with grief.

sentences.zh: 以軍勞累授沁州刺史，遷衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: For military merit he was repeatedly appointed Prefect of Qinzhou, then promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was repeatedly appointed Prefect of Qinzhou, then promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 口陳願治民，試一縣自效，除河東令，寬猛時當。

translations.literal: He stated orally his wish to govern the people and asked to try his ability in one county; he was appointed Magistrate of Hedong, and his balance of leniency and severity was always appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: He stated orally his wish to govern the people and asked to try his ability in one county; he was appointed Magistrate of Hedong, and his balance of leniency and severity was always appropriate.

sentences.zh: 由蘄州刺史遷安南經略使。

translations.literal: From Prefect of Qi Prefecture he was transferred to Commissioner for Pacifying the South in Annan.
translations.idiomatic: From Prefect of Qi Prefecture he was transferred to Commissioner for Pacifying the South in Annan.

sentences.zh: 環王國叛人李樂山謀廢其君，來乞兵，行立不受，命部將杜英策討斬之，歸其孥，蠻人悅服。

translations.literal: Li Leshan, a rebel of the Huanwang kingdom, plotted to depose his ruler and came to beg troops; Xingli refused. He ordered his subordinate general Du Yingce to attack and behead him, returned his wife and children, and the barbarians submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Leshan, a rebel of the Huanwang kingdom, plotted to depose his ruler and came to beg troops; Xingli refused. He ordered his subordinate general Du Yingce to attack and behead him, returned his wife and children, and the barbarians submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 英策及範廷芝者，皆谿洞豪也，隸於軍，它經略使多假借，暴恣幹治，行立陰把其罪，貸之，許自效，故能得英策死力。

translations.literal: Yingce and Fan Tingzhi were both powerful men of the stream-and-cave districts who were subordinated to the army; other commissioners for pacification often borrowed them and, violent and willful, interfered in governance. Xingli secretly grasped their crimes, pardoned them, and allowed them to redeem themselves through service; thus he could obtain Yingce's utmost loyalty even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Yingce and Fan Tingzhi were both powerful men of the stream-and-cave districts who were subordinated to the army; other commissioners for pacification often borrowed them and, violent and willful, interfered in governance. Xingli secretly grasped their crimes, pardoned them, and allowed them to redeem themselves through service; thus he could obtain Yingce's utmost loyalty even unto death.

sentences.zh: 廷芝嘗休沐，久不還，行立召之，約曰：「軍法，逾日者斬，異時復然，爾且死！

translations.literal: Once when Tingzhi took leave, he did not return for a long time. Xingli summoned him and warned: "Under military law, one who is overdue is to be executed. If this happens again, you will die!
translations.idiomatic: Once when Tingzhi took leave, he did not return for a long time. Xingli summoned him and warned: "Under military law, one who is overdue is to be executed. If this happens again, you will die!

sentences.zh: 」後廷芝逾期，行立笞殺之，以屍還範氏，更為擇良子弟以代，於是威聲風行。

translations.literal: " Later Tingzhi was overdue; Xingli had him flogged to death and returned the corpse to the Fan clan, then selected a worthy younger kinsman to replace him. Thereafter his authority and reputation spread like the wind.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Tingzhi was overdue; Xingli had him flogged to death and returned the corpse to the Fan clan, then selected a worthy younger kinsman to replace him. Thereafter his authority and reputation spread like the wind.

sentences.zh: 徙桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner as Observer of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commissioner as Observer of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 黃家洞賊叛，行立討平之。

translations.literal: When the Huangjiadong bandits rebelled, Xingli suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huangjiadong bandits rebelled, Xingli suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 俄代桂仲武為安南都護。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Gui Zhongwu as Protector-General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Gui Zhongwu as Protector-General of Annan.

sentences.zh: 銳於立功，為時所訾。

translations.literal: Keen to achieve merit, he was criticized by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Keen to achieve merit, he was criticized by people of the time.

sentences.zh: 召還，道卒，年四十七，贈右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was recalled and died on the road at the age of forty-seven; he was posthumously given the post of Right Regular Attendant at the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and died on the road at the age of forty-seven; he was posthumously given the post of Right Regular Attendant at the Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 崔沔，字善沖，京兆長安人，後周隴州刺史士約四世孫，自博陵徙焉。

translations.literal: Cui Hao, style name Shanchong, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao; he was a fourth-generation descendant of Shi Yue, Governor of Long in the Later Zhou, and his family had moved thither from Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, style name Shanchong, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao; he was a fourth-generation descendant of Shi Yue, Governor of Long in the Later Zhou, and his family had moved thither from Boling.

sentences.zh: 純謹無二言，事親篤孝，有才章。

translations.literal: Pure and careful, never speaking a careless word; in serving his parents he was deeply filial and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and careful, never speaking a careless word; in serving his parents he was deeply filial and had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 擢進士。

translations.literal: He was selected as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as jinshi.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正高第，不中者誦訾之，武後敕有司覆試，對益工，遂為第一。

translations.literal: In the examination for Worthy and Upright with outstanding achievement, those who failed slandered him. Empress Wu ordered the authorities to retest him; his answers were even more polished, and he took first place.
translations.idiomatic: In the examination for Worthy and Upright with outstanding achievement, those who failed slandered him. Empress Wu ordered the authorities to retest him; his answers were even more polished, and he took first place.

sentences.zh: 再補陸渾主簿，入調吏部，侍郎岑義嘆曰：「君今郤詵也！

translations.literal: After a second appointment as Registrar of Luhun, he entered for transfer at the Ministry of Personnel; Vice Minister Cen Yi exclaimed: "Sir, you are today's Xi Shen!
translations.idiomatic: After a second appointment as Registrar of Luhun, he entered for transfer at the Ministry of Personnel; Vice Minister Cen Yi exclaimed: "Sir, you are today's Xi Shen!

sentences.zh: 」薦為左補闕。

translations.literal: " He was recommended as Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: " He was recommended as Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 性舒遲，進止雍如也，當官則正言，不可得而詘。

translations.literal: By nature unhurried, his movements and pauses were dignified; when he held office he spoke uprightly and could not be bent aside.
translations.idiomatic: By nature unhurried, his movements and pauses were dignified; when he held office he spoke uprightly and could not be bent aside.

sentences.zh: 睿宗召授中書舍人，以母病東都不忍去，固辭求侍，更表陸渾尉郭鄰、太樂丞封希顏、處士李喜以代己處。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong summoned him and appointed him Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, but because his mother was ill in the eastern capital he could not bear to leave and firmly declined, asking to attend her; he further memorialized that Guo Lin, Registrar of Luhun, Feng Xiyan, Assistant Director of the Imperial Music Office, and the recluse Li Xi might replace him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong summoned him and appointed him Drafting Attendant of the Secretariat, but because his mother was ill in the eastern capital he could not bear to leave and firmly declined, asking to attend her; he further memorialized that Guo Lin, Registrar of Luhun, Feng Xiyan, Assistant Director of the Imperial Music Office, and the recluse Li Xi might replace him in office.

sentences.zh: 詔改虞部郎中，俄檢校御史中丞。

translations.literal: An edict changed his post to Doctor of the Office of Parks and Manufactories, and soon he was made Acting Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict changed his post to Doctor of the Office of Parks and Manufactories, and soon he was made Acting Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 請發太倉粟及減苑囿鳥獸所給以賑貧乏，人賴其利。

translations.literal: He requested that grain from the ever-normal granaries be released and that supplies to birds and beasts from the imperial parks be reduced to relieve the poor; people benefited from his policy.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that grain from the ever-normal granaries be released and that supplies to birds and beasts from the imperial parks be reduced to relieve the poor; people benefited from his policy.

sentences.zh: 監察御史宋宣遠與盧懷慎姻家，恃以弄法；

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Song Xuanyuan was related by marriage to Lu Huaishen and relied on that connection to manipulate the law;
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Song Xuanyuan was related by marriage to Lu Huaishen and relied on that connection to manipulate the law;

sentences.zh: 姚崇子彜留司東都，通賓客，招賄賂。

translations.literal: Yao Chong's son Yi, staying behind as chief in the eastern capital, entertained guests freely and solicited bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong's son Yi, staying behind as chief in the eastern capital, entertained guests freely and solicited bribes.

sentences.zh: 沔將按劾，崇、懷慎方執政，共薦沔有史才，轉著作郎，去其權，蓋憚之也。

translations.literal: Hao was about to investigate and impeach them. Chong and Huaishen were then in power and together recommended Hao as having talent for historiography, transferring him to Compiler, thereby removing his authority—essentially because they feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was about to investigate and impeach them. Chong and Huaishen were then in power and together recommended Hao as having talent for historiography, transferring him to Compiler, thereby removing his authority—essentially because they feared him.

sentences.zh: 久之，為太子左庶子。

translations.literal: After a long while he became Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he became Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 母亡，受吊廬前，賓客未嘗至柩室。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he received mourners in the mourning hut; guests never entered the chamber of the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he received mourners in the mourning hut; guests never entered the chamber of the coffin.

sentences.zh: 語人曰：「平生非至親不升堂入謁，豈以存亡變禮邪？

translations.literal: He told people: "In life I never ascended the hall or paid a visit except to the closest kin—should I change ritual because of life and death?
translations.idiomatic: He told people: "In life I never ascended the hall or paid a visit except to the closest kin—should I change ritual because of life and death?

sentences.zh: 」中書令張說數稱之。

translations.literal: " Chief Minister Zhang Yue often praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " Chief Minister Zhang Yue often praised him.

sentences.zh: 服除，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以仙州數喪刺史，欲廢之，沔請治舞陽，舞陽，故樊噲國也，更為樊州，帝不納，州卒廢。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, because several governors of Xian Prefecture had died in office, wished to abolish it. Hao asked to govern Wuyang—Wuyang being the former state of Fan Kuai—and rename it Fan Prefecture. The Emperor did not accept it; the prefecture was eventually abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong, because several governors of Xian Prefecture had died in office, wished to abolish it. Hao asked to govern Wuyang—Wuyang being the former state of Fan Kuai—and rename it Fan Prefecture. The Emperor did not accept it; the prefecture was eventually abolished.

sentences.zh: 沔既喜論得失，或曰：「今中書宰相承制，雖侍郎貳之，取充位而已。

translations.literal: Because Hao delighted in discussing right and wrong, someone said: "Today the Secretariat Chancellor receives imperial decrees; although the Vice Minister assists, one merely fills the post.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hao delighted in discussing right and wrong, someone said: "Today the Secretariat Chancellor receives imperial decrees; although the Vice Minister assists, one merely fills the post.

sentences.zh: 」沔曰：「百官分職，上下相維，以成至治，豈可俯首懷祿邪？

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Officials each have their duties; superiors and subordinates mutually support one another to achieve the highest governance—how can one bow one's head and clutch one's salary?
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "Officials each have their duties; superiors and subordinates mutually support one another to achieve the highest governance—how can one bow one's head and clutch one's salary?

sentences.zh: 」凡詔敕曹事，多所異同，說不悅，出為魏州刺史。

translations.literal: " Whenever drafting edicts and handling Secretariat affairs involved many differences, Yue was displeased and sent him out as Prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever drafting edicts and handling Secretariat affairs involved many differences, Yue was displeased and sent him out as Prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 雨潦敗稼，沔弛禁便人。

translations.literal: When heavy rains ruined the crops, Hao relaxed prohibitions to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: When heavy rains ruined the crops, Hao relaxed prohibitions to benefit the people.

sentences.zh: 召還。

translations.literal: He was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled.

sentences.zh: 分掌吏部十銓，以左散騎常侍為集賢修撰，歷秘書監、太子賓客。

translations.literal: He shared responsibility for the ten selection boards of the Ministry of Personnel, served as Left Regular Attendant at the Palace Gate in the compilation of the Imperial Library, and successively held the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He shared responsibility for the ten selection boards of the Ministry of Personnel, served as Left Regular Attendant at the Palace Gate in the compilation of the Imperial Library, and successively held the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是時，太常議加宗廟籩豆，又欲增喪服，於是卿韋縚請坐增籩豆至十二；

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Temple deliberated increasing the bamboo bean vessels in the ancestral temple and also wished to expand mourning garments. Therefore Vice Minister Wei Yun requested that the supplemental vessels be increased to twelve;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Grand Temple deliberated increasing the bamboo bean vessels in the ancestral temple and also wished to expand mourning garments. Therefore Vice Minister Wei Yun requested that the supplemental vessels be increased to twelve;

sentences.zh: 外祖服大功，舅小功，堂姨若舅、舅母袒免。

translations.literal: mourning for maternal grandparents in the major mourning grade, for uncles on the mother's side in the lesser mourning grade, and for paternal aunts as for uncles and for maternal uncles and aunts the bared-shoulder mourning without full garments.
translations.idiomatic: mourning for maternal grandparents in the major mourning grade, for uncles on the mother's side in the lesser mourning grade, and for paternal aunts as for uncles and for maternal uncles and aunts the bared-shoulder mourning without full garments.

sentences.zh: 沔曰：「祭祀上矣，古者飲食必先嚴獻。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Sacrifice is supreme. In antiquity one always first made a solemn offering before eating.
translations.idiomatic: Hao said: "Sacrifice is supreme. In antiquity one always first made a solemn offering before eating.

sentences.zh: 未有火化，故有毛血之薦，未有曲糵，故有玄酒之奠。

translations.literal: Before the discovery of fire, there were offerings of hair and blood; before the discovery of fermentation, there were libations of dark liquor.
translations.idiomatic: Before the discovery of fire, there were offerings of hair and blood; before the discovery of fermentation, there were libations of dark liquor.

sentences.zh: 後王作為酒醴、犧牲以致馨香，故有三牲、八簋、五齊、九獻。

translations.literal: Later kings created wine and grain liquor and victims to bring fragrance; hence the three victims, the eight gui vessels, the five clarified liquors, and the nine presentations.
translations.idiomatic: Later kings created wine and grain liquor and victims to bring fragrance; hence the three victims, the eight gui vessels, the five clarified liquors, and the nine presentations.

sentences.zh: 神道主敬，可備而不敢廢也，雖曰備物，而節制存焉。

translations.literal: The way of the spirits is grounded in reverence: what may be provided must not be abandoned through neglect, and though one speaks of fully providing things, restraint is preserved within.
translations.idiomatic: The way of the spirits is grounded in reverence: what may be provided must not be abandoned through neglect, and though one speaks of fully providing things, restraint is preserved within.

sentences.zh: 钘俎、籩豆、簠簋尊罍之實，皆周時饌，其用通宴饗賓客，而周公與毛血、玄酒同薦於先祖。

translations.literal: The filling of the offering stand, the bamboo vessels, and the gui and bo vessels and wine jars—all were Zhou-period foods, used commonly for feasts and entertaining guests—yet the Duke of Zhou presented them together with hair-and-blood and dark liquor before the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The filling of the offering stand, the bamboo vessels, and the gui and bo vessels and wine jars—all were Zhou-period foods, used commonly for feasts and entertaining guests—yet the Duke of Zhou presented them together with hair-and-blood and dark liquor before the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 晉盧諶家祭禮，所薦皆晉時常食，不純用古。

translations.literal: In the Jin period, Lu Chen's family sacrificial rites offered all foods that were regular fare in Jin times, not purely using ancient ones.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin period, Lu Chen's family sacrificial rites offered all foods that were regular fare in Jin times, not purely using ancient ones.

sentences.zh: 此聖賢變文而通其情也。

translations.literal: This is how sages and worthies changed the text to express their meaning and meet the situation.
translations.idiomatic: This is how sages and worthies changed the text to express their meaning and meet the situation.

sentences.zh: 然當時飲食不可闕於祭，明矣。

translations.literal: Yet it is clear that the diet of the time could not be omitted from sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it is clear that the diet of the time could not be omitted from sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 國家清廟時享，禮饌具設，周制也，古物存焉。

translations.literal: When the state offers seasonal sacrifices in the Clear Temple, ritual foods are fully set out—that is Zhou practice, and ancient things are preserved therein.
translations.idiomatic: When the state offers seasonal sacrifices in the Clear Temple, ritual foods are fully set out—that is Zhou practice, and ancient things are preserved therein.

sentences.zh: 園寢上食，時膳備列，漢法也，它珍極焉。

translations.literal: In the park-tombs, superior offerings and timely banquet provisions are fully arrayed—that is Han practice, with other delicacies at their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: In the park-tombs, superior offerings and timely banquet provisions are fully arrayed—that is Han practice, with other delicacies at their utmost.

sentences.zh: 職貢來祭，致遠物也。

translations.literal: Tribute from duty offices arriving for sacrifice brings distant products.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute from duty offices arriving for sacrifice brings distant products.

sentences.zh: 有新必薦，順時令也。

translations.literal: Whenever there is something new it must be offered—that follows the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever there is something new it must be offered—that follows the seasons.

sentences.zh: 苑囿躬稼所收，搜狩親中，莫不薦而後食，盡誠敬民。

translations.literal: What is harvested from the imperial parks through personal plowing, what is caught in personal hunts—none is eaten before being offered; utmost sincerity and respect for the people.
translations.idiomatic: What is harvested from the imperial parks through personal plowing, what is caught in personal hunts—none is eaten before being offered; utmost sincerity and respect for the people.

sentences.zh: 若此至矣，無以加矣。

translations.literal: If it reaches this point, nothing can be added.
translations.idiomatic: If it reaches this point, nothing can be added.

sentences.zh: 諸珍羞鮮物，第敕有司悉使著於令，因宜而薦，不必加籩豆以為嗛也。

translations.literal: For all delicacies and fresh things, simply order the relevant offices to set them down in regulations and offer them as appropriate; there is no need to add bamboo vessels merely out of modesty.
translations.idiomatic: For all delicacies and fresh things, simply order the relevant offices to set them down in regulations and offer them as appropriate; there is no need to add bamboo vessels merely out of modesty.

sentences.zh: 大羹，古食也，盛於古器。

translations.literal: Da geng is ancient food, served in ancient vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Da geng is ancient food, served in ancient vessels.

sentences.zh: 和羹，常饌也，盛於時器。

translations.literal: He geng is ordinary fare, served in vessels of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonized broth is everyday food, served in contemporary vessels.

sentences.zh: 毛血盛於盤，玄酒盛於尊。

translations.literal: Hair and blood are placed in platters; dark liquor is placed in wine vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Hair and blood belong in platters; dark liquor belongs in goblets.

sentences.zh: 未有薦時饌而用古器者，繇古質而今文，便事也。

translations.literal: There has never been offering seasonal fare while using ancient vessels; from antiquity's plainness to the present's refinement, convenience governs.
translations.idiomatic: No one has ever offered seasonal foods in ancient vessels—from the plainness of old times to the refinement of today, what matters is what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 故加籩豆未足盡天下美物，而措諸朝，徒近侈耳。

translations.literal: Therefore adding basket-and-bean vessels still cannot exhaust all fine things under Heaven, and to set them out at court merely draws one near to extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Adding more ritual baskets and stands still could not display every delicacy under Heaven; to parade them at court would be nothing but a step toward extravagance.

sentences.zh: 魯丹桓宮之楹，刻其桷，《春秋》非之。

translations.literal: When Lu carved the pillars of Duke Huan's shrine and ornamented the rafter-ends, the Spring and Autumn Annals condemned it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Lu carved the pillars of Duke Huan's ancestral temple and decorated the rafter-ends, the Spring and Autumn Annals censured him for it.

sentences.zh: 班固稱：『墨家出於清廟，是以貴儉。

translations.literal: Ban Gu stated: 『The Mohists arose from the Clear Temple; therefore they value frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu wrote: 『The Mohist school took its origin in the Clear Temple, and for that reason honors thrift.

sentences.zh: 』然清廟不奢，舊矣。

translations.literal: 』Yet the Clear Temple has not been lavish—that is the old way.
translations.idiomatic: 』Yet the Clear Temple itself has never been lavish; that has been true since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 太常所請，臣所未安。」

translations.literal: What the Grand Temple has requested is something with which your minister is not yet at ease.」
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Temple's proposal is something your minister cannot yet accept with confidence.」

sentences.zh: 又太常言：「爵小不及合，執持至難。

translations.literal: Again the Grand Temple said: 「The jue cup is so small it cannot hold a full measure, and it is extremely difficult to hold.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Temple also argued: 「The jue cup is too small to hold a full measure and is very hard to carry.

sentences.zh: 」沔曰：「禮有以小為貴者，獻以爵是也。

translations.literal: 」Hao said: 「In ritual there are cases where small is honored; presenting with the jue cup is such a case.
translations.idiomatic: 」Hao replied: 「Ritual sometimes honors what is small; offering wine with the jue cup is exactly such a case.

sentences.zh: 然今不及制，則非禮，自有司之陋也。

translations.literal: However, if the present cups cannot meet the specification, that is not ritual—it is the deficiency of the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: But if today's cups fail to meet the proper standard, that is not ritual at all—it is simply the incompetence of the offices charged with the task.

sentences.zh: 隨失制宜，不待議而革雲。

translations.literal: One adapts measures to deficiencies; reform need not await deliberation before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Adjust what is lacking and fashion what is appropriate; reform need not wait for endless debate.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「禮本於家正，家正而天下定。

translations.literal: 」He also said: 「Ritual takes root in correct family order; when the family is ordered, all under Heaven is settled.
translations.idiomatic: 」He went on: 「Ritual begins with proper order in the family; when the family is in order, the realm is stable.

sentences.zh: 家不可以貳，故父以尊崇，母以厭降。

translations.literal: A family cannot have two heads; therefore the father is honored by elevation and the mother is honored by deferential lowering.
translations.idiomatic: A household cannot have two masters; hence the father is honored by elevation and the mother by reverent deference.

sentences.zh: 是以內服齊斬，外服緦，尊名所加，不過一等，今古不易之道也。

translations.literal: Thus for internal kin one wears qi and zhan mourning, for external kin si mourning; honor added to a title goes no further than one grade—this is a Way unchanged from antiquity to the present.
translations.idiomatic: That is why close kin wear qi and zhan mourning while more distant kin wear si mourning, and the honor conferred by a title may rise by only one degree—a principle unchanged from ancient times to our own.

sentences.zh: 昔辛有適伊川，見被發而祭，知其將戎，禮先亡也。

translations.literal: In the past Xinyou, passing through Yichuan, saw people with loose hair performing sacrifice and knew barbarians would come—ritual had perished first.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Xinyou, traveling through Yichuan, saw people with unbound hair making sacrifice and knew barbarians were coming—ritual had already collapsed.

sentences.zh: 比制《唐禮》，推廣舅恩，故弘道以來，國命再移於外姓，本禮驗亡，可不戒哉！

translations.literal: When the Tang Rites were recently formulated, maternal-uncle kindness was broadened; hence since the Hongdao era the imperial mandate has twice shifted to outside surnames—the root ritual verified as lost—can one not be warned!
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang Rites were recently codified, mourning for maternal uncles was extended; since the Hongdao era the throne has twice passed to outsiders—a proof that the root ritual was already lost. Should we not take warning!

sentences.zh: 」時職方郎中韋述、戶部郎中陽伯成、禮部員外郎楊仲昌、監門兵曹參軍劉秩等議與沔合，又詔中書門下參裁，於是宗廟籩豆坐各六，姨若舅小功，舅母緦麻，堂姨袒免，余仍舊制。

translations.literal: 」At the time Director of Duty Offices Wei Shu, Director of the Ministry of Revenue Yang Bocheng, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites Yang Zhongchang, Army Section Officer of the Gate Guard Liu Zhi, and others agreed with Hao; the emperor also ordered the Central Secretariat and Chancellery to adjudicate. Thereupon the ancestral temple had six basket-and-bean vessels at each setting; maternal aunts were treated like maternal uncles in lesser mourning, maternal uncles' wives in finest hemp mourning, and paternal female cousins in bared-shoulder mourning without full garments; the rest remained under the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: 」At the time Wei Shu of the Duty Office, Yang Bocheng of the Ministry of Revenue, Yang Zhongchang of the Ministry of Rites, Liu Zhi of the Gate Guard, and others sided with Hao; the throne also ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to decide the matter. In the end each ancestral setting kept six basket-and-bean vessels; maternal aunts received the same lesser mourning as maternal uncles, maternal uncles' wives received finest hemp mourning, and paternal female cousins received bared-shoulder mourning, while everything else stayed under the old rules.

sentences.zh: 每朝廷有疑議，皆咨逮取衷。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had doubtful deliberations, all consulted Hao to obtain a decisive view.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court faced a disputed question, it consulted Hao to settle on a final decision.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十七，贈禮部尚書，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-seven, was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, and was given the posthumous title Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven, was posthumously made Minister of Rites, and received the posthumous name Xia, Filial.

sentences.zh: 沔儉約自持，祿稟隨散宗族，不治居宅，嘗作《陋室銘》以見誌。

translations.literal: Hao maintained frugal self-restraint, distributed salary and grain rations among the clan as they came, did not maintain a residence, and once wrote Inscription on a Humble Chamber to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hao lived frugally and held himself to strict restraint, giving away his salary and grain rations to the clan as soon as they arrived; he kept no fine house and once wrote Inscription on a Humble Chamber to declare his convictions.

sentences.zh: 子祐甫至宰相，別傳。

translations.literal: His son Youfu rose to Chancellor; treated in a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Youfu rose to chancellor; he is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 盧從願，字子龔。

translations.literal: Lu Congyuan, style name Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congyuan, courtesy name Zigong.

sentences.zh: 六世祖昶，仕後魏為度支尚書，自范陽徙臨漳，故從願為臨漳人。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Chang served the Later Wei as Minister of Revenue; moving from Fanyang to Linzhang, hence Congyuan was a native of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Chang served the Northern Wei as Minister of Revenue; the family moved from Fanyang to Linzhang, so Congyuan was a native of Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，為夏尉。

translations.literal: Selected through the Mingjing examination, he became magistrate of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed magistrate of Xia.

sentences.zh: 又舉制科高第，拜右拾遺，遷監察御史，為山南黜陟巡撫使，還奏稱旨，累進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He also scored top on the special decree examination, was appointed Reminder of the Right, was promoted to Investigating Censor, served as Dismissal-and-Promotion Commissioner for Shannan, returned with memorials pleasing to the throne, and was repeatedly promoted to Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He also placed at the top of a special decree examination, was made Reminder of the Right, rose to Investigating Censor, served as Dismissal-and-Promotion Commissioner for Shannan, and on his return submitted memorials that pleased the emperor; he was then promoted repeatedly until he became Drafting Secretary of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 吏選自中宗後綱紀耗蕩，從願精力於官，偽牒詭功，擿檢無所遺，銓總六年，以平允聞。

translations.literal: After Zhongzong, personnel selection's rules and discipline were worn down and dissipated; Congyuan applied his energy to the office, exposing forged credentials and false merit claims with nothing missed; over six years of overseeing selection he was known for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhongzong, the rules governing appointments had fallen into disorder; Congyuan threw himself into the work, exposing forged documents and false claims of merit without missing a case. Over six years in charge of selection he became known for evenhanded fairness.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，特官其一子。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at this and specially granted an office to one of his sons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and specially granted office to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 從願請贈其父敬一為鄭州長史，制可。

translations.literal: Congyuan requested posthumous appointment for his father Jingyi as Prefect of Zhengzhou; the edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Congyuan asked that his father Jingyi be posthumously appointed Prefect of Zhengzhou, and the edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗時，吏部號稱職者裴行儉、馬載，及是，從願與李朝隱為有名，故號「前有裴、馬，後有盧、李」。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Gaozong's time, those praised as capable at the Ministry of Personnel were Pei Xingjian and Ma Zai; at this time Congyuan and Li Chaoyin were famous, so they were called "Before, Pei and Ma; after, Lu and Li."
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Gaozong's day the Ministry of Personnel had been praised for the competence of Pei Xingjian and Ma Zai; now Congyuan and Li Chaoyin won equal renown, and people said, "Before there were Pei and Ma; afterward there are Lu and Li."

sentences.zh: 開元四年，玄宗悉召縣令策於廷，考下第者罷之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, Xuanzong summoned all magistrates to policy examinations at court and dismissed those who ranked at the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 4 Emperor Xuanzong summoned every county magistrate to an imperial policy examination and removed those who failed.

sentences.zh: 從願坐擬選失實，下遷豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Congyuan was demoted for nominating appointments that did not match reality and was transferred down to be Prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Congyuan was punished because some of his nominations proved false and was demoted to Prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 政嚴簡，奏課為天下第一，寶書勞問，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: His governance was stern yet simple; his memorial assessments ranked first in the empire; the emperor sent a letter of commendation and bestowed one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was strict but uncluttered; his annual report ranked first in the empire, and the emperor sent a letter of praise and granted him one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 召為工部侍郎，遷尚書左丞、中書侍郎，以工部尚書留守東都，代韋抗為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Recalled as Vice Minister of Works, he was promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director of the Secretariat; as Minister of Works he remained at the Eastern Capital; he replaced Wei Kang as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Vice Minister of Works, then promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director of the Secretariat; as Minister of Works he remained at the Eastern Capital, and later replaced Wei Kang as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 數充校考使，升退詳確。

translations.literal: Several times he served as examination commissioner; promotions and demotions were detailed and accurate.
translations.idiomatic: He served several times as examination commissioner, and his decisions on promotion and demotion were thorough and precise.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞宇文融方用事，將以括田戶功為上下考，從願不許，融恨之，乃密白「從願盛殖產，占良田數百頃」，帝自此薄之，目為多田翁。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong was then in power and wanted to use land-registration household results as the basis for upper and lower annual assessments; Congyuan did not permit it. Rong resented him and secretly reported that "Congyuan has aggressively expanded estates, occupying several hundred qing of good farmland." From this the emperor came to think less of him and called him the Old Man of Many Fields.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong was then in power and wanted annual ratings to depend on the results of his land-registration campaign; Congyuan refused. Rong bore a grudge and secretly reported that "Congyuan has amassed estates and seized several hundred qing of good farmland." From then on the emperor thought less of him and nicknamed him the Old Man of Many Fields.

sentences.zh: 後欲用為相屢矣，卒以是止。

translations.literal: Later the emperor several times wished to use him as chancellor, but in the end stopped on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor several times meant to make him chancellor, but in the end always stopped because of this.

sentences.zh: 十八年，復為東都留守，坐子起居郎論輸糴於官取利多，貶絳州刺史，遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he again served as Eastern Capital Intendant; because his son Lun, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, had sold grain to the government at excessive profit, he was demoted to Prefect of Jiangzhou and transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he again served as Eastern Capital Intendant; because his son Lun, an attendant of the heir apparent, had sold grain to the government at excessive profit, he was demoted to Prefect of Jiangzhou and then made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十年，河北饑，詔為宣撫處置使，發倉廥賑饑民。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when Hebei suffered famine, he was ordered as Pacification and Disposition Commissioner, opening granaries to relieve the hungry people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, when Hebei suffered famine, he was appointed Pacification and Disposition Commissioner and opened the granaries to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 使還，乞骸骨，授吏部尚書致仕，給全祿終身。

translations.literal: When the mission ended he requested retirement; was appointed Minister of Personnel with permission to retire, granted full salary for life.
translations.idiomatic: When his mission ended he asked to retire; he was made Minister of Personnel with permission to leave office and granted his full salary for life.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈益州大都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He died; was posthumously made Great Governor-General of Yizhou; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Great Governor-General of Yizhou with the posthumous name Wen, Cultured.

sentences.zh: 李朝隱，字光國，京兆三原人。

translations.literal: Li Chaoyin, style name Guangguo, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chaoyin, courtesy name Guangguo, was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 明法中第，調臨汾尉，擢至大理丞。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingfa examination with high rank, was assigned as magistrate of Linfen, and was promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He placed high on the Mingfa examination, was assigned as magistrate of Linfen, and rose to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 武三思構五王，而侍御史鄭愔請誅之，朝隱獨以「不經鞫實，不宜輕用法」，忤旨，貶嶺南醜地。

translations.literal: When Wu Sansi framed the Five Princes and Attending Censor Zheng Yin requested their execution, Chaoyin alone argued that "without interrogation and verification one should not lightly apply the law," contravening the imperial wish; he was demoted to an ugly place in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sansi framed the Five Princes and Attending Censor Zheng Yin asked that they be executed, Chaoyin alone objected that "without trial and verified facts the law should not be applied lightly," defying the imperial will; he was banished to a remote place in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 宰相韋巨源、李嶠言於中宗曰：「朝隱素清正，一日遠逐，恐駭天下。

translations.literal: Chancellors Wei Juyuan and Li Jiao said to Zhongzong: 「Chaoyin has always been upright and incorrupt; to banish him far in a single day will surely alarm all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors Wei Juyuan and Li Jiao said to Emperor Zhongzong: 「Chaoyin has always been upright; to banish him overnight would shock the realm.

sentences.zh: 」帝更以為聞喜令。

translations.literal: 」The emperor then reappointed him magistrate of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor then reassigned him as magistrate of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史、吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attending Censor and Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Censor and Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時政出權幸，不關兩省而內授官，但斜封其狀付中書，即宣所司。

translations.literal: At the time policy issued from powerful favorites; appointments not passing through the two secretariats but internally conferred—merely slant-sealing their documents and delivering them to the Central Secretariat, which would announce the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: At the time power lay with favored courtiers; appointments bypassed the two secretariats and were made by private decree—the documents were simply slant-sealed and sent to the Central Secretariat, which then announced them to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 朝隱執罷千四百員，怨誹歡騰，朝隱胖然無避屈。

translations.literal: Chaoyin enforced cancellation of fourteen hundred positions; resentment and calumny boiled over, yet Chaoyin remained boldly unflinching without evasion or yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin enforced the removal of fourteen hundred appointees; resentment and slander erupted everywhere, yet he remained composed and unyielding, never shrinking from the task.

sentences.zh: 遷長安令，宦官閭興貴有所幹請，曳去之。

translations.literal: Promoted to magistrate of Chang'an, when eunuch Lu Xinggui made a private request he dragged him away.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to magistrate of Chang'an, he once had eunuch Lu Xinggui dragged away when the man tried to press a private request on him.

sentences.zh: 睿宗嘉嘆，後禦承天門，對百官及朝集使褒諭其能，使遍聞之。

translations.literal: Ruizong admired and exclaimed over this; later at Chengtian Gate he addressed the hundred officials and assembly envoys, praising his ability and having it broadcast widely.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong praised him warmly; later, at Chengtian Gate, he addressed the officials and provincial envoys, commended Chaoyin's conduct, and had the praise spread throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 進太中大夫一階，賜中上考、絹百匹，以旌剛烈。

translations.literal: He was advanced one step in Grand Masters of the Palace, granted upper-middle annual assessment and one hundred bolts of silk, to commend his stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin was promoted one rank to Grand Master of the Palace, given an upper-middle performance rating and one hundred bolts of silk, in recognition of his stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 成安公主奪民園，不酬直，朝隱取主奴杖之，由是權豪斂伏。

translations.literal: Princess Cheng'an seized a commoner's garden without paying compensation; Chaoyin had the princess's slaves caned, whereupon the powerful and wealthy submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Cheng'an seized a commoner's garden without paying fair value, Chaoyin had the princess's servants beaten with the rod, and from then on the powerful families kept their heads down.

sentences.zh: 為執政所擠，出通州都督，徙絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Squeezed out by those in power, he went out as Military Governor of Tongzhou and was moved to Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pushed aside by those in power, he was sent out as Military Governor of Tongzhou and later transferred to Prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遷吏部侍郎，銓敘明審，與盧從願並授一子官。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel; his review and ordering were clear and exact; together with Lu Congyuan each was granted an office for a son.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he became Vice Minister of Personnel; his evaluations were clear and exact, and he and Lu Congyuan were each granted office for a son.

sentences.zh: 久之，以策縣令有下第，降滑州刺史，徙同州。

translations.literal: After some time, because policy examinations of magistrates had failures, he was demoted to Prefect of Hua and moved to Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, because some county magistrates he had recommended failed their policy examinations, he was demoted to Prefect of Hua and then transferred to Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 玄宗東幸，召見慰勞，賜以衣、帛。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong traveled east, he was summoned, consoled, and rewarded with clothing and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong traveled east, he summoned Chaoyin, comforted him, and granted him clothing and silk.

sentences.zh: 擢河南尹，政嚴清，奸人不容息。

translations.literal: Promoted to Governor of Henan; his governance was stern and clean; evil men had no place to rest.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Governor of Henan; his rule was strict and clean, and wrongdoers found no refuge.

sentences.zh: 太子舅趙常奴怙勢橫閭裏，朝隱曰：「此不繩，不可為政。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent's maternal uncle Zhao Changnu relied on influence and rampaged through the lanes; Chaoyin said: 「If this is not punished by law, one cannot govern.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's maternal uncle Zhao Changnu abused his connections and terrorized the neighborhood; Chaoyin said: 「If men like this are not restrained by law, there can be no government.

sentences.zh: 」執而搒辱之，帝賜書慰勉。

translations.literal: 」He seized him and had him beaten and humiliated; the emperor sent a letter of consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: 」He had him seized, beaten, and publicly shamed; the emperor then sent a letter praising and encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 入為大理卿。

translations.literal: He entered court service as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 武強令裴景仙丐贓五千匹，亡命，帝怒，詔殺之。

translations.literal: Pei Jingxian, magistrate of Wuqiang, embezzled five thousand bolts of silk and fled; the emperor in anger ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jingxian, magistrate of Wuqiang, embezzled five thousand bolts of silk and fled; the emperor in anger ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 朝隱曰：「景仙，其先寂有國功，載初時，家為酷吏所破，誅夷略盡，而景仙獨存，且承嫡，於法當請。

translations.literal: Chaoyin said: 「Jingxian's ancestor Ji had merit establishing the state; in the Zaichu period his family was destroyed by harsh officials, with near-total execution, yet Jingxian alone survived; moreover he was the legitimate heir—in law he should be permitted to plead.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin said: 「Jingxian's ancestor Pei Ji helped found the dynasty; in the Zaichu era his family was ruined by harsh officials and nearly wiped out, yet Jingxian alone survived as the legitimate heir. Under the law he should be allowed to plead for mercy.

sentences.zh: 又丐乞贓無死比，藉當死坐，猶將宥之，使私廟之祀無餒魂可也。

translations.literal: Further, embezzlement has no statute requiring death; if even one deserving death is still to be pardoned, then private ancestral temples need not lack offerings for hungry souls.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, embezzlement carries no mandatory death penalty; even when a capital offense might apply, mercy is still possible, so that private ancestral rites need not go unperformed for want of an heir.

sentences.zh: 」帝不許，固請曰：「生殺之柄，人主專之；

translations.literal: 」The emperor did not assent; he firmly pleaded: 「The power of life and death belongs solely to the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor refused, but Chaoyin pressed on: 「The power of life and death belongs to the ruler alone;

sentences.zh: 條別輕重，有司當守。

translations.literal: distinguishing lighter and heavier penalties is what the offices must uphold.
translations.idiomatic: but distinguishing lighter from heavier penalties is what the offices must uphold.

sentences.zh: 且贓惟枉法抵死，今丐贓即斬，後有枉法，亦又何加？

translations.literal: And only bending the law reaches death for embezzlement; if embezzling merit pay means immediate execution, then for later bending the law what further penalty remains?
translations.idiomatic: Only corruption through bending the law carries the death penalty; if mere embezzlement now means immediate execution, what punishment remains for the graver crime of bending the law?

sentences.zh: 且近發德音，杖者聽減，流者給程，豈一景仙獨過常法？

translations.literal: Moreover a recent amnesty edict permitted reduction for those flogged and granted travel funds for those exiled—how could Jingxian alone exceed the regular law?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a recent amnesty allowed commutation for those sentenced to beating and travel funds for those exiled—why should Jingxian alone be treated more harshly than the law allows?

sentences.zh: 」有詔決杖百，流嶺南。

translations.literal: 」An edict was issued: one hundred blows with the rod, exile to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: 」An edict was issued sentencing him to one hundred blows with the rod and exile to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 朝隱更授岐州刺史，母喪解。

translations.literal: Chaoyin was again appointed Prefect of Qi and resigned on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin was again appointed Prefect of Qi, then left office when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 召為揚州大都督府長史，固辭，見聽。

translations.literal: Summoned as Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, he firmly declined and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture, firmly declined, and was allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 時年已衰，而篤於孝，自致毀瘠，士人以為難。

translations.literal: By then he was already aged, yet deep in filial piety; he brought himself to emaciation through mourning; scholars regarded this as difficult to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was already old, yet so devoted in filial piety that he wore himself to emaciation in mourning; scholars admired this as hard to match.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔書敦遣揚州就職。

translations.literal: The next year an edict urgently dispatched him to take office at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict urgently ordered him to take up his post at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還為大理卿，封金城伯，代崔隱甫為御史大夫。

translations.literal: He returned as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, was enfeoffed as Baron of Jincheng, and replaced Cui Yinpu as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, was enfeoffed as Baron of Jincheng, and replaced Cui Yinpu as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 天下以其有素望，每大夫缺，冀朝隱得之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven, because of his longstanding reputation, whenever the chief censor's post was vacant hoped Chaoyin would obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his long-standing reputation, whenever the post of censor-in-chief fell vacant the realm expected Chaoyin to receive it.

sentences.zh: 及居職，不爭引大體，惟先細務，由是名少衰。

translations.literal: Once in office, he did not contend for great principles but always put minor affairs first; hence his reputation slightly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, however, he no longer pressed broad principles but gave priority to minor matters, and his reputation waned somewhat.

sentences.zh: 進太常卿，出為嶺南采訪處置使，兼判廣州。

translations.literal: Promoted to Grand Master of Ceremonials, he was sent out as Pacification and Disposition Commissioner for Lingnan, concurrently administering Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Grand Master of Ceremonials, he was sent out as Pacification and Disposition Commissioner for Lingnan and concurrently administered Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，贈吏部尚書，官給車槥北還，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died in office; was posthumously made Minister of Personnel; the government provided cart and coffin for return north; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, was posthumously made Minister of Personnel, and the government provided a cart and coffin for his return north; his posthumous name was Zhen, Upright.

sentences.zh: 王丘，字仲山，同交從子也。

translations.literal: Wang Qiu, style name Zhongshan, was a younger clansman of the same collateral branch.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu, courtesy name Zhongshan, was a younger cousin within the clan.

sentences.zh: 父同至，終太子左庶子。

translations.literal: His father Tongzhi ultimately served as Left Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tongzhi ended his career as Left Vice Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 丘十一擢童子科，它童皆專經，而獨屬文，由是知名。

translations.literal: At eleven Qiu passed the child prodigy examination; the other children all specialized in classics while he alone excelled at literature—thereby he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven Wang Qiu passed the child prodigy examination; the other boys all focused on the classics while he alone excelled at literary composition, and from that he became well known.

sentences.zh: 及冠，舉制科中第，授奉禮郎。

translations.literal: At capping age he passed the decree examination and was appointed Gentleman of Ceremonials.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he passed a decree examination and was appointed Gentleman for Ceremonial Duties.

sentences.zh: 氣象清古，行修絜，於詞賦尤高。

translations.literal: His bearing was clear and antique, his conduct refined and pure; he was especially distinguished in fu and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing was clear and dignified, his conduct refined and pure, and he was especially accomplished in fu and rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 族人方慶及魏元忠更薦之，自偃師主簿擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Clansmen Wang Fangqing and Wei Yuanzhong repeatedly recommended him; from Magistrate of Yanshi he was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Wang Fangqing and Wei Yuanzhong repeatedly recommended him, and he rose from Magistrate of Yanshi to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 開元初，遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan he was promoted to Vice Director of the Department of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era he became Vice Director in the Department of Merit.

sentences.zh: 考功異時多請托，進者濫冒，歲數百人。

translations.literal: The Department of Merit at that time saw much patronage; appointees were numerous and unqualified, several hundred each year.
translations.idiomatic: The Department of Merit had long been subject to patronage; unqualified candidates passed in the hundreds every year.

sentences.zh: 丘務核實材，登科才滿百，議者謂自武後至是數十年，采錄精明無丘比。

translations.literal: Qiu strove to verify actual talent; those passing the examination barely reached one hundred; discussants said that from Empress Wu until then, spanning several decades, selection had never been as sharp and precise as under Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu insisted on verifying real talent; fewer than a hundred passed that year, and commentators said that in the decades since Empress Wu's time no selection had been as sharp and exacting as his.

sentences.zh: 其後席豫、嚴挺之亦有稱，然出丘下。

translations.literal: Afterwards Xi Yu and Yan Tingzhi also had reputations, but fell short of Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xi Yu and Yan Tingzhi also won praise, but neither matched Qiu.

sentences.zh: 遷紫微舍人、吏部侍郎，典選，復號平允。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafter at the Palace Library and Vice Minister of Personnel; in charge of selection, he was again famed for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Drafter at the Palace Library and Vice Minister of Personnel; put in charge of selection, he again became known for fairness.

sentences.zh: 其獎用如山陰尉孫逖、桃林尉張鏡微、湖城尉張晉明、進士王泠然，皆一時茂秀。

translations.literal: Those he rewarded and employed, such as Shan'yin Magistrate Sun Ti, Taolin Magistrate Zhang Jingwei, Hucheng Magistrate Zhang Jinming, and jinshi graduate Wang Lingran, were all outstanding talents of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Those he promoted and employed—including Sun Ti, magistrate of Shan'yin; Zhang Jingwei, magistrate of Taolin; Zhang Jinming, magistrate of Hucheng; and jinshi graduate Wang Lingran—were all brilliant men of their generation.

sentences.zh: 久之，為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 會山東旱饑，議以中朝臣為刺史，制詔：「臯陶稱：『在知人，在安民。

translations.literal: When Shandong suffered drought and famine, it was deliberated to appoint central-court ministers as prefects; an edict stated: 「Gao Yao said: 『Know men, and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong suffered drought and famine, the court decided to send central officials out as prefects; an edict declared: 「Gao Yao said: 『In knowing men and in settling the people

sentences.zh: 』皆念存邦本，朝乾夕惕，無忘一日。

translations.literal: 』Both thoughts hold fast to the foundation of the state—diligent morning and evening, never forgetting it for a day.
translations.idiomatic: 』lie the foundations of the state. Morning and evening be diligent and watchful, and never forget this for a single day.

sentences.zh: 今長吏或未稱，蒼生謂何？

translations.literal: If local chiefs now fail to measure up, what will the common people say?
translations.idiomatic: If the local chiefs are unworthy, what will the common people do?

sentences.zh: 深思循良，以革頹敝，宜重刺史之選，自朝廷始。

translations.literal: Deeply consider the good and honest, to reform decline and corruption—the selection of prefects should be weighted heavily, beginning at court.
translations.idiomatic: Think deeply on good and honest officials to reform decay and neglect; the choice of prefects should be taken seriously, beginning here at court.

sentences.zh: 」乃以丘與中書付郎崔沔等並為山東刺史。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon Qiu together with Vice Director of the Secretariat Cui Hao and others were all appointed prefects of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: 」Thereupon Wang Qiu, together with Cui Hao, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and others were all appointed prefects in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 而丘守懷州，尤清嚴，為下畏慕。

translations.literal: Qiu governed Huaizhou especially with clarity and severity; those below both feared and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu governed Huaizhou with especial clarity and severity; those under him both feared and admired him.

sentences.zh: 入知吏部選，改尚書左丞，以父喪解。

translations.literal: Recalled to manage personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel, he was changed to Left Assistant Director; he resigned on his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to oversee personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel, he was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, then left office when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服除，為右散騎常侍，仍知制誥。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was appointed Right Regular Attendant, still drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed Right Regular Attendant and continued to draft imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 裴光庭卒，蕭嵩與丘善，將引與當國，丘固辭，盛推韓休行能。

translations.literal: Pei Guangting died; Xiao Song was on good terms with Qiu and planned to bring him in to handle state affairs, but Qiu firmly declined and enthusiastically recommended Han Xiu's capability.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Guangting died, Xiao Song, who was close to Wang Qiu, intended to bring him into power to run the government. Qiu firmly refused and instead strongly recommended Han Xiu's ability.

sentences.zh: 及休秉政，薦為御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Han Xiu took hold of government, he recommended him as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Once Han Xiu came to power, he recommended Qiu for the post of Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 丘訥於言，所白奏帝多不喜，改太子賓客，襲父封。

translations.literal: Qiu was slow of speech; memorials he submitted the Emperor mostly disliked. He was changed to Mentor of the Crown Prince and inherited his father's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu was reticent in speech, and the Emperor often disliked the memorials he submitted. He was reassigned as Mentor of the Crown Prince and inherited his father's noble title.

sentences.zh: 以疾徙禮部尚書，致仕。

translations.literal: On account of illness he was transferred to Minister of Rites and retired.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he was moved to the post of Minister of Rites and then retired from office.

sentences.zh: 丘更履華劇，而所守清約，未嘗通饋遺，室宅童騎敝陋，既老，藥餌不自給。

translations.literal: Qiu's posts became ever more splendid and weighty, yet what he upheld was purity and frugality; he never accepted gifts. His house, servants, and mounts were shabby and worn; in old age he could not even provide his own medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wang Qiu rose to ever more exalted and demanding offices, he lived by strict frugality and never accepted gifts. His home, servants, and horses were plain and worn, and in his old age he could scarcely afford his own medicine.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆之，以謂有古人節，下制給全祿以旌絜吏。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed over this, saying he had the integrity of the ancients, and issued an edict granting full salary to honor an incorrupt official.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sighed and said that Qiu possessed the integrity of men of old. He issued an edict granting him full salary in recognition of an incorrupt official.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年卒，贈荊州大都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao he died; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Protector-General of Jingzhou, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Tianbao. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Protector-General of Jingzhou and given the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 嚴挺之，名浚，以字行，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Yan Tingzhi, personal name Jun, was known by his courtesy name; a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Tingzhi, whose personal name was Jun but who was known by his courtesy name, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少好學，姿質軒秀。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; his bearing and appearance were lofty and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning, and his bearing and appearance were strikingly handsome.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，並擢制科，調義興尉，號材吏。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was also selected in the decree examination; appointed magistrate of Yixing, and called a talented official.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was also selected through the decree examination. Appointed magistrate of Yixing, he was known as a capable official.

sentences.zh: 姚崇為州刺史，異之。

translations.literal: When Yao Chong was prefect of the province, he regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong served as prefect of the province, he took special notice of him.

sentences.zh: 崇執政，引為右拾遺。

translations.literal: When Chong took power, he introduced him as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yao Chong came to power, he brought him in as Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 侍御史任正名恃風憲，至廷中責詈衣冠，挺之讓其不敬，反為所劾，貶萬州員外參軍事。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Ren Zhengming relied on his disciplinary authority; he went into the court and scolded officials in their robes and caps. Tingzhi reproached him for disrespect, but in turn was impeached by him and demoted to supernumerary staff member at Wanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Ren Zhengming abused his disciplinary authority, going into court to berate officials in their robes and caps. Tingzhi rebuked him for disrespect, but Ren impeached him in return, and he was demoted to supernumerary staff member at Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為考功員外郎，累進給事中，典貢舉，時號平允。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he served as Vice Director in the Department of Merit, was promoted step by step to Attendant-in-Ordinary, and managed the tribute examinations; at the time he was famed for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he served as Vice Director in the Department of Merit, rose through successive promotions to Attendant-in-Ordinary, and oversaw the civil examinations. At the time he was known for fairness.

sentences.zh: 會杜暹、李元纮為相，不相中。

translations.literal: When Du Xuan and Li Yuanhong served as chancellors, they did not get along.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Xuan and Li Yuanhong served together as chancellors, the two did not get along.

sentences.zh: 暹善挺之，而元纮善宋遙，用為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Xuan favored Tingzhi, while Yuanhong favored Song Yao; he was appointed Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xuan favored Tingzhi, while Li Yuanhong favored Song Yao. Tingzhi was appointed Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遙校吏部判，取舍與挺之異，言於元纮，元纮屢詰譙，挺之厲言曰：「公位相國，而愛憎反任小人乎？

translations.literal: Yao checked the Ministry of Personnel decisions; his selections differed from Tingzhi's. He spoke of this to Yuanhong, and Yuanhong repeatedly interrogated and reproached him.
