Tingzhi spoke sharply, saying: 「You hold the rank of chief minister, yet let love and hate be decided by petty men instead?
translations.idiomatic: Song Yao reviewed the Ministry of Personnel decisions, and his choices differed from Tingzhi's. He reported this to Li Yuanhong, who repeatedly questioned and berated Tingzhi. Tingzhi spoke sharply: 「You hold the rank of chief minister—do you really let your likes and dislikes be decided by petty men?

sentences.zh: 」元纮曰：「小人為誰？

translations.literal: 」Yuanhong said: 「Who is the petty man?
translations.idiomatic: 」Li Yuanhong asked, 「Who is the petty man?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「宋遙也。

translations.literal: 」He said: 「Song Yao.
translations.idiomatic: 」He answered, 「Song Yao.

sentences.zh: 」由是出為登州刺史，改太原少尹。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he was sent out as Prefect of Dengzhou and then changed to Vice Governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: 」Because of this he was sent out as Prefect of Dengzhou and later transferred to Vice Governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，殿中監王毛仲持節抵太原朔方籍兵馬，後累年，仍移太原取兵仗，挺之不肯應，且以毛仲寵幸，久恐有變，密啟於帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, Director of the Palace Domestic Service Wang Maozhong, bearing credentials, reached Taiyuan and Shuofang to register troops and horses. In later years he still came to Taiyuan to obtain weapons and armor. Tingzhi refused to comply, and because Maozhong enjoyed imperial favor, fearing trouble over time, he secretly reported to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Maozhong, Director of the Palace Domestic Service, had come with imperial credentials to Taiyuan and Shuofang to register troops and horses. Years later he still came to Taiyuan to demand weapons and armor. Tingzhi refused to comply. Fearing that Maozhong's long-held favor might one day lead to trouble, he secretly reported the matter to the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 俄改濮、汴二州刺史，所治皆嚴威，吏至重足脅息。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Prefect of Pu and Bian; everywhere he governed was strict and severe, and officials walked on tiptoe, holding their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to serve as prefect of Pu and Bian. His rule in both places was strict and severe, and officials were so intimidated that they walked on tiptoe and hardly dared breathe.

sentences.zh: 會毛仲敗死，帝以挺之言忠，召為刑部侍郎，遷太府卿。

translations.literal: When Maozhong failed and died, the Emperor considered Tingzhi's words loyal and summoned him as Vice Minister of Justice, then promoted him to Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozhong fell from power and died, the Emperor regarded Tingzhi's earlier report as loyal and recalled him as Vice Minister of Justice, then promoted him to Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 宰相張九齡雅知之，用為尚書左丞，知吏部選。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhang Jiuling had long known him well and appointed him Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, in charge of personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhang Jiuling had long known and respected him. He appointed him Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and put him in charge of personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 李林甫與九齡同輔政，以九齡方得君，諂事之，內實不善也。

translations.literal: Li Linfu jointly assisted governance with Jiuling; because Jiuling had just gained the ruler's favor, Linfu flattered and served him, yet inwardly he truly disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu served alongside Zhang Jiuling as co-regent. Because Jiuling had only recently won the Emperor's favor, Linfu flattered him outwardly while inwardly disliking him.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎蕭炅，林甫所引，不知書，嘗與挺之言，稱蒸嘗伏臘，乃為「伏獵」。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Xiao Jiong, whom Linfu had promoted, was unlearned. Once, speaking with Tingzhi, he referred to sacrificial offerings at the seasonal festivals of Fuxi and said instead 「crouching hunt.」
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Xiao Jiong, a man Li Linfu had promoted, was illiterate. Once, speaking with Tingzhi, he meant to refer to sacrificial offerings at the seasonal festivals of Fuxi and La, but said 「crouching hunt」 instead.

sentences.zh: 挺之白九齡：「省中而有伏獵侍郎乎！

translations.literal: Tingzhi told Jiuling: 「Can there be a Crouching-Hunt Vice Minister in the Secretariat!
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi reported to Zhang Jiuling, 「Can the Secretariat really have a 'Crouching-Hunt' vice minister?

sentences.zh: 」乃出炅岐州刺史，林甫恨之。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon Jiong was sent out as Prefect of Qizhou, and Linfu resented him for it.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xiao Jiong was then sent out as Prefect of Qizhou, and Li Linfu resented Tingzhi for it.

sentences.zh: 九齡欲引以輔政，使往謁林甫，挺之負正，陋其為人，凡三年，非公事不造也，林甫益怨。

translations.literal: Jiuling wished to bring him in to assist governance and had him go pay respects to Linfu. Tingzhi was upright by nature and despised Linfu's character; for three years, unless on official business he would not visit, and Linfu grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling wanted to bring Tingzhi into the inner circle of government and had him go pay a visit to Li Linfu. Tingzhi was upright by nature and despised Linfu's character. For three years he never called on Linfu except on official business, and Linfu's resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 會挺之有所諉於蔚州刺史王元琰，林甫使人暴其語禁中，下除洺州刺史，徙絳州。

translations.literal: When Tingzhi had some grievance against Wei Prefect Wang Yuanyan, Linfu had men expose his words inside the palace. He was demoted and sent out as Prefect of Mingzhou, then transferred to Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzhi had a grievance against Wang Yuanyan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, Li Linfu had his words exposed inside the palace. Tingzhi was demoted to Prefect of Mingzhou and then transferred to Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，帝顧林甫曰：「嚴挺之安在？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao the Emperor turned to Linfu and said: 「Where is Yan Tingzhi?
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianbao era the Emperor turned to Li Linfu and asked, 「Where is Yan Tingzhi?

sentences.zh: 此其材可用。

translations.literal: His talent can be used.
translations.idiomatic: His talent is still worth using.

sentences.zh: 」林甫退召其弟損之與道舊，諄諄款曲，且許美官，因曰：「天子視絳州厚，要當以事自解歸，得見上，且大用。

translations.literal: 」Linfu withdrew and summoned his younger brother Sun Zhi to speak of old times, warmly and at length, and also promised him a fine office. He then said: 「The Son of Heaven regards Jiang Prefecture as important; you must resolve matters on your own and return, see the Emperor, and then be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: 」Li Linfu withdrew and summoned his younger brother Sun Zhi to reminisce with him, speaking warmly and at length and promising him a fine office. Then he said, 「The Son of Heaven thinks highly of your service in Jiang Prefecture. You should resolve your affairs there, return home, see the Emperor, and then you will be greatly promoted.

sentences.zh: 」因紿挺之使稱疾，願就醫京師。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he deceived Tingzhi into claiming illness and wishing to seek medical treatment in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 」He then tricked Tingzhi into reporting illness and asking to go to the capital for medical treatment.

sentences.zh: 林甫已得奏，即言挺之春秋高，有疾，幸閑官得自養。

translations.literal: Linfu had already obtained the memorial and immediately said that Tingzhi was advanced in years, had illness, and would be fortunate to receive an idle post where he could nourish himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu had already received the memorial and immediately reported that Tingzhi was old and ill and would be better off with an idle post where he could recuperate.

sentences.zh: 帝恨咤久之，乃以為員外詹事，詔歸東都。

translations.literal: The Emperor lamented angrily for a long time, then appointed him Supernumerary Household Tutor and ordered him to return to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fumed for a long time, then appointed Tingzhi Supernumerary Household Tutor and ordered him back to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 挺之郁郁成疾，乃自為文誌墓，遺令薄葬，斂以時服。

translations.literal: Tingzhi, depressed, fell ill. He then wrote his own epitaph, left instructions for a simple burial, and to be enshrouded in everyday dress.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi grew despondent and fell ill. He wrote his own epitaph, left instructions for a simple burial, and directed that he be laid out in everyday clothes.

sentences.zh: 挺之重交遊，許與生死不易，嫁故人孤女數十人，當時重之。

translations.literal: Tingzhi valued friendship; he pledged bonds unchanging through life and death and married off dozens of orphaned daughters of old friends. People of the time respected him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi valued friendship deeply. He pledged bonds that would not change in life or death and saw dozens of orphaned daughters of old friends married off. People of the time greatly respected him for this.

sentences.zh: 然溺誌於佛，與浮屠惠義善，義卒，衰服送其喪，已乃自葬於其塔左，君子以為偏。

translations.literal: Yet he was drowned in devotion to Buddhism; he was close to the monk Huiyi. When Huiyi died, he wore mourning and attended the funeral, then had himself buried to the left of Huiyi's pagoda. Men of principle regarded this as excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was obsessed with Buddhism and was close to the monk Huiyi. When Huiyi died, Tingzhi wore mourning and attended his funeral, then arranged to be buried beside the left side of Huiyi's pagoda. Men of principle thought this excessive.

sentences.zh: 子武。

translations.literal: His son was Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yan Wu.

sentences.zh: 武，字季鷹。

translations.literal: Wu, courtesy name Jiying.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, courtesy name Jiying.

sentences.zh: 幼豪爽。

translations.literal: From childhood he was bold and generous.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was bold and open-handed.

sentences.zh: 母裴不為挺之所答，獨厚其妾英。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Pei, was not treated as she deserved by Tingzhi; he favored only his concubine Ying.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Pei, was neglected by Tingzhi, who favored only his concubine Ying.

sentences.zh: 武始八歲，怪問其母，母語之故。

translations.literal: When Wu was only eight, he asked in puzzlement about this; his mother told him the reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu was only eight years old, he asked his mother about it in puzzlement, and she told him why.

sentences.zh: 武奮然以鐵錘就英寢，碎其首。

translations.literal: Wu, stirred to anger, took an iron hammer to Ying's bedchamber and smashed her head.
translations.idiomatic: Wu seized an iron hammer, went to Ying's bedchamber in a fury, and smashed her skull.

sentences.zh: 左右驚白挺之曰：「郎戲殺英。

translations.literal: Those around him, startled, reported to Tingzhi: 「The young master playfully killed Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him rushed to tell Tingzhi in alarm, 「The young master killed Ying in play.

sentences.zh: 」武辭曰：「安有大臣厚妾而薄妻者，兒故殺之，非戲也。

translations.literal: 」Wu replied: 「How can there be a great minister who favors a concubine and slighted his wife? Your son therefore killed her—it was no play.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wu answered, 「How can a great minister favor a concubine and neglect his wife? I killed her on purpose—it was no accident.

sentences.zh: 」父奇之，曰：「真嚴挺之子！

translations.literal: 」His father marveled at this and said: 「Truly a son of Yan Tingzhi!
translations.idiomatic: 」His father was astonished and said, 「A true son of Yan Tingzhi!

sentences.zh: 」然數禁敕。

translations.literal: 」Yet he repeatedly forbade and admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: 」Even so, he repeatedly forbade and admonished him.

sentences.zh: 武讀書不甚究其義，以蔭調太原府參軍事，累遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Wu in reading did not greatly pursue the meaning of texts. By yin privilege he was appointed staff member of the Taiyuan prefecture and was promoted step by step to Attending Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu did not study books deeply enough to grasp their meaning. Through hereditary privilege he entered service as a staff member in the Taiyuan prefecture and rose step by step to Attending Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 從玄宗入蜀，擢諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Xuanzong into Shu, he was promoted to Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Emperor Xuanzong into Shu, he was promoted to Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 至德初，赴肅宗行在，房琯以其名臣子，薦為給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he went to Emperor Suzong's mobile court. Fang Guan, because he was the son of a famed minister, recommended him as Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhide era he went to Emperor Suzong's mobile court. Fang Guan, considering him the son of a famous minister, recommended him for the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 已收長安，拜京兆少尹。

translations.literal: After Chang'an had been recovered, he was appointed Vice Governor of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chang'an had been recovered, he was appointed Vice Governor of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 坐琯事貶巴州刺史。

translations.literal: On account of Fang Guan's affair he was demoted to Prefect of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Fang Guan's disgrace he was demoted to Prefect of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷東川節度使。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Military Governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to Military Governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 上皇合劍南為一道，擢武成都尹、劍南節度使。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor merged Jiannan into one circuit and promoted Wu to Governor of Chengdu and Military Governor of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor merged Jiannan into a single circuit and promoted Wu to Governor of Chengdu and Military Governor of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 還，拜京兆尹，為二聖山陵橋道使，封鄭國公。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Governor of the Capital District, made Commissioner for the Bridge Roads of the Two Sages' Imperial Tombs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Governor of the Capital District, made Commissioner for the Bridge Roads of the Two Sages' Imperial Tombs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 與元載厚相結，求宰相不遂，復節度劍南。

translations.literal: He formed a close bond with Yuan Zai; seeking the chancellorship without success, he again became military governor of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a close alliance with Yuan Zai. When his bid for the chancellorship failed, he returned to serve again as military governor of Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 破吐藩七萬眾於當狗城，遂收鹽川。

translations.literal: He defeated seventy thousand Tibetan troops at Dangou Fort and then recovered Yanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated seventy thousand Tibetan troops at Dangou Fort and then recovered Yanchuan.

sentences.zh: 加檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 武在蜀頗放肆，用度無藝，或一言之悅，賞至百萬。

translations.literal: Wu in Shu was quite unrestrained; his expenditures knew no limit, and sometimes for a single pleasing remark he would reward as much as a million.
translations.idiomatic: In Shu, Wu was quite unrestrained. His spending knew no bounds, and sometimes a single pleasing remark would earn a reward of as much as a million cash.

sentences.zh: 蜀雖號富饒，而峻掊亟斂，閭裏為空，然虜亦不敢近境。

translations.literal: Although Shu was called rich and fertile, he harshly scraped and urgently levied taxes until neighborhoods were emptied; yet the barbarians also did not dare approach the border.
translations.idiomatic: Although Shu was known as rich and fertile, he taxed it harshly and relentlessly until whole neighborhoods were drained empty. Even so, the enemy did not dare approach the border.

sentences.zh: 梓州刺史章彜始為武判官，因小忿殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, Prefect of Zizhou, had first served as Wu's judge; over a small grievance Wu killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, prefect of Zizhou, had once served as Wu's aide. Over a minor quarrel Wu had him killed.

sentences.zh: 琯以故宰相為巡內刺史，武慢倨不為禮。

translations.literal: Fang Guan, as a former chancellor, served as an itinerant inspector within the circuit; Wu was arrogant and did not show him courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan, a former chancellor, came as an itinerant inspector within the circuit, but Wu treated him with arrogant disrespect.

sentences.zh: 最厚杜甫，然欲殺甫數矣。

translations.literal: He was closest to Du Fu, yet several times he wanted to kill Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He was closest to Du Fu, yet more than once he wanted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 李白為《蜀道難》者，乃為房與杜危之也。

translations.literal: That Li Bai wrote 「Hard Road to Shu」 was to warn Fang and Du of danger.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bai wrote 「Hard Road to Shu」 to warn Fang Guan and Du Fu of the danger they faced.

sentences.zh: 永泰初卒，母哭，且曰：「而今而後，吾知免為官婢矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai he died. His mother wept and said: 「From now on, I know I am spared becoming a government maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Yongtai era. His mother wept and said, 「From now on I know I am spared becoming a government maidservant.

sentences.zh: 」年四十，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: 」He was forty years old; posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: 」He was forty years old. He was posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 挺之從孫綬。

translations.literal: Tingzhi's collateral grandson was Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi's collateral grandson was Yan Shou.

sentences.zh: 綬父丹，嘗為劍南鹽鐵、青苗、租庸使，以武在蜀，辭不拜。

translations.literal: Shou's father Dan had once served as Commissioner for Salt and Iron, Green Sprouts, and Tax Corvée in Jiannan; because Wu was in Shu, he declined the appointment and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's father Dan had once been appointed Commissioner for Salt and Iron, Green Sprouts, and Tax Corvée in Jiannan, but because Yan Wu was in Shu he declined the post and never took it up.

sentences.zh: 綬擢進士第，以侍御史副劉贊為宣歙團練使。

translations.literal: Shou passed the jinshi examination and, as Attending Censor, served as deputy to Liu Zan, Regiment Training Commissioner of Xuan-She.
translations.idiomatic: Shou passed the jinshi examination and served as Attending Censor under Liu Zan, Regiment Training Commissioner of Xuan-She.

sentences.zh: 贊卒，綬總留事，悉庫物以獻，召為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Zan died, Shou took charge of remaining affairs, presented all treasury goods as tribute, and was summoned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zan died, Shou took charge of affairs and sent all the treasury goods to the court as tribute. He was then recalled and appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 賓佐進奉由綬始。

translations.literal: Staff members' tribute submissions began with Shou.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of staff members sending tribute to the throne began with Shou.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使李說病，軍司馬鄭儋總其政，說卒，代為節度。

translations.literal: Military Governor of Hedong Li Shuo fell ill; Army Vice Commissioner Zheng Dan took charge of his administration. When Shuo died, Dan replaced him as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuo, Military Governor of Hedong, fell ill, and Army Vice Commissioner Zheng Dan took over the administration. When Shuo died, Dan succeeded him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 時德宗務姑息，方鎮若帥死，不它命，即用軍司馬代之，以和厭眾情。

translations.literal: At the time Dezong pursued an indulgent policy: if a frontier governor died, without another appointment the army vice commissioner was immediately used to replace him, in order to appease the troops' sentiments.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Dezong pursued a conciliatory policy toward the frontier. When a military governor died, the court often made no other appointment but simply let the army vice commissioner succeed him, so as to appease the troops.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝頗憶綬所獻，故擢為河東司馬。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor rather remembered what Shou had presented, and therefore promoted him to Army Vice Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the Emperor still remembered Shou's earlier tribute and therefore promoted him to Army Vice Commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 明年，儋卒，即檢校工部尚書，代其使。

translations.literal: The next year, when Dan died, he was immediately appointed Acting Minister of Works and replaced him as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Zheng Dan died, Shou was immediately appointed Acting Minister of Works and succeeded him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，楊惠琳反夏州，劉辟反蜀，綬建言：「天子始即位，不可失威，請必誅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, Yang Huilin rebelled at Xia Prefecture and Liu Bi rebelled in Shu. Shou submitted advice: 「The Son of Heaven has just ascended; authority must not be lost—please be sure to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne, Yang Huilin rebelled at Xia Prefecture and Liu Bi rebelled in Shu. Shou advised, 「The Son of Heaven has just ascended the throne and cannot afford to lose authority. I ask that they be put to death without fail.

sentences.zh: 」選銳兵，遣大將李光顏助討賊。

translations.literal: 」He selected crack troops and sent the great general Li Guangyan to assist in suppressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: 」He selected crack troops and sent the great general Li Guangyan to help suppress the rebels.

sentences.zh: 二賊平，檢校尚書左僕射，封扶風郡公，進司空。

translations.literal: When the two rebels were pacified, he was appointed Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery, and advanced to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After both rebellions were put down, he was appointed Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffed as Duke of Fufeng Commandery, and promoted to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 在鎮九年，尚寬惠，治稱流聞，士馬孳息。

translations.literal: He remained at his post nine years, still generous and mild; his governance was famed far and wide, and troops and horses multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at his post for nine years, governing with generosity and mildness. His reputation spread widely, and both troops and horses increased in number.

sentences.zh: 嘗大閱，旗幟周七十里，回鶻梅錄將軍在會，聞金鼓震伏。

translations.literal: Once, during a grand review, banners and flags extended for seventy li around; the Uyghur Meilu General was present at the assembly, and hearing the drums and gongs he trembled and cowered.
translations.idiomatic: Once, during a grand review, banners and flags stretched for seventy li around the field. The Uyghur Meilu General was present, and when he heard the thunder of drums and gongs he trembled and cowered.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 綬既名胄，於吏事有方略，然銳進趣，素議薄之。

translations.literal: Shou, being of famous lineage, had strategy in administrative affairs, yet he was keen to advance; public opinion had long looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shou came from a distinguished family and handled administrative affairs with skill, but he was eager to advance, and public opinion had long looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 始就廊下食，在百官上，帝使中人賜含桃，綬見拜之，為御史劾奏，綬慚懼待罪，詔釋綬而貶中人。

translations.literal: Just as he began eating in the corridor, above the hundred officials, the Emperor had a eunuch grant him cherries. Shou saw this and bowed to the eunuch. A censor impeached him; Shou, ashamed and fearful, awaited punishment. An edict pardoned Shou and demoted the eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he began eating in the corridor, seated above the other officials, the Emperor sent a eunuch to grant him cherries. Shou saw this and bowed to the eunuch. A censor impeached him. Shou, ashamed and afraid, awaited punishment. An edict pardoned Shou and demoted the eunuch instead.

sentences.zh: 出為荊南節度使，封鄭國公。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Military Governor of Jingnan and enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Military Governor of Jingnan and enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 漵州蠻張伯靖殺吏，據辰、錦州，連九洞自固，詔綬進討。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou barbarian Zhang Bojing killed officials, seized Chen and Jin prefectures, linked nine cave settlements to fortify himself, and an edict ordered Shou to advance and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bojing, a tribal leader of Xuzhou, killed officials and seized Chen and Jin prefectures, linking nine cave settlements to hold his ground. An edict ordered Shou to advance against him.

sentences.zh: 綬勒兵出次，遣將賫檄開曉，群蠻悉降。

translations.literal: Shou marshaled troops and moved out to camp, sent a general bearing proclamations to enlighten them, and all the barbarian groups submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shou marshaled his troops and moved out to encamp, then sent a general with proclamations to explain the court's will. All the tribal groups submitted.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟反，僉以綬明恕可大事，乃徙山南東道節度使，加淮西招撫使。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji rebelled, all agreed that Shou's clarity and leniency suited a great undertaking; he was therefore transferred to Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit and additionally made Pacification Commissioner of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji rebelled, everyone agreed that Shou's mild and forgiving manner suited a major pacification effort. He was transferred to Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit and additionally made Pacification Commissioner of Huai West.

sentences.zh: 綬引師壓賊境，多出金帛賞士，以厚賂謝中人，招聲援，既未有以制賊，閉屯彌年不戰。

translations.literal: Shou led his army to press the rebel border, greatly dispensed gold and silk to reward soldiers, and with heavy bribes thanked eunuchs to solicit vocal support. Yet having no means to subdue the rebels, he closed camp and for a full year did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Shou led his army up to the rebel border, lavished gold and silk on his soldiers, and gave heavy bribes to eunuchs to win their public support. Yet he had no effective way to defeat the rebels and kept his camp closed for a full year without fighting.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴度謂綬非將才，以太子少保召還，檢校司徒，判光祿卿事，進少傅。

translations.literal: Chancellor Pei Du said Shou was not a general's talent; he was recalled as Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, appointed Acting Minister of Education, assigned the duties of Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and advanced to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Pei Du said Shou lacked the talent of a general. He was recalled as Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, appointed Acting Minister of Education, assigned the duties of Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and promoted to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十七，贈太保。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-seven years of age; posthumously appointed Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-seven and was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 綬才不逾中人，然歷三鎮，所奏辟及綬時位將相者九人。

translations.literal: Shou's talent did not surpass an ordinary man, yet having served three military posts, those he memorialized and recruited, together with those who at Shou's time held rank as chancellor or general, numbered nine men.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's talent was no more than middling, yet over three military postings the men he recommended and recruited included nine who later rose to chancellor or general.

sentences.zh: 初，綬未顯，過於闅鄉尉李達，達不禮，方飯它客，不召綬。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Shou had risen to prominence, he passed the home of Weixiang Magistrate Li Da. Da did not treat him courteously; he was just dining other guests and did not summon Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shou had risen to prominence, he once passed the home of Li Da, magistrate of Weixiang. Da treated him discourteously: he was entertaining other guests and did not invite Shou to join them.

sentences.zh: 後達罷彭城令，過并州，晨入謁，不知綬也。

translations.literal: Later, when Da had left office as magistrate of Pengcheng and passed through Bingzhou, he came early in the morning to pay respects, not knowing it was Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Da had left office as magistrate of Pengcheng, he passed through Bingzhou and came early in the morning to pay his respects, not realizing that the man he was calling on was Shou.

sentences.zh: 綬方大宴賓客，召達至，戒客勿起，讓曰：「吾昔羈旅闅鄉，君方召客食而不顧我，今我召客亦不敢留君。

translations.literal: Shou was just holding a great banquet for guests. He summoned Da forward, warned the guests not to rise, and reproached him, saying: 「In the past I was a traveler stranded at Weixiang; you were inviting guests to dine and paid no heed to me. Now that I am inviting guests, I likewise dare not keep you.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was holding a grand banquet for his guests. He summoned Da forward, told the guests not to rise, and reproached him: 「When I was a stranded traveler in Weixiang, you were entertaining guests and paid no attention to me. Now that I am entertaining guests, I likewise dare not keep you.

sentences.zh: 」達慚，不得去，左右引出，悸而瘖，臥館數月，其佐令狐楚為請，乃免。

translations.literal: 」Da was ashamed and could not leave; attendants led him out. He was frightened into muteness and lay bedridden in the lodge for several months. His aide Linghu Chu pleaded on his behalf, and only then was he spared.
translations.idiomatic: 」Da was ashamed but could not leave. Attendants led him out. He was so frightened that he lost his voice and lay bedridden in the guest lodge for months. His aide Linghu Chu pleaded for him, and only then was he spared further punishment.

sentences.zh: 河東李進賢者，善畜牧，家高貲，得幸於綬，署牙門將。

translations.literal: There was Li Jinxian of Hedong, skilled in animal husbandry, from a wealthy family; gaining Shou's favor, he was appointed Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man of Hedong named Li Jinxian, skilled in animal husbandry and from a wealthy family. Favored by Shou, he was appointed Gate General.

sentences.zh: 元和中，進賢累為振武節度使，辟綬子澈為判官。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era Jinxian repeatedly served as Military Governor of Zhenwu and recruited Shou's son Che as judge.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era Li Jinxian served repeatedly as Military Governor of Zhenwu and recruited Shou's son Che as his aide.

sentences.zh: 澈年少，治苛刻，軍中苦之。

translations.literal: Che was young; in governing he was harsh and exacting, and the army suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: Che was still young, and his rule was harsh and exacting; the troops found him unbearable.

sentences.zh: 回鶻入辟鵜泉，進賢發兵討之，吏廩糧不實，次鳴砂，焚殺其將楊遵憲而還。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs entered Bipiquan; Jinxian raised troops to attack them. The officials' granary provisions were not as reported; he halted at Mingsha, burned and killed his general Yang Zunxian, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs raided Bipiquan, Jinxian mobilized troops against them. The commissary grain turned out short of what had been reported; he camped at Mingsha, executed his general Yang Zunxian by fire, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進賢大怒，眾懼，因燔城門，攻進賢，左右拒戰不勝，縋而去，奔靖邊軍。

translations.literal: Jinxian was greatly enraged; the troops were afraid. Thereupon they set fire to the city gate and attacked Jinxian. His attendants resisted but could not prevail; he was lowered by rope and fled, running to the Jingbian army.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxian flew into a rage, and the men were terrified. They burned the city gate and turned on him. His guards fought back but were beaten; he was lowered over the wall by rope and escaped to the Jingbian garrison.

sentences.zh: 乃殺澈而屠進賢家。

translations.literal: They then killed Che and slaughtered Jinxian's entire household.
translations.idiomatic: They then killed Che and massacred everyone in Jinxian's family.

sentences.zh: 詔以夏綏銀節度使張煦代之，誅亂首數百人乃定。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhang Xu, Military Governor of Xia-Sui-Yin, to replace him; after executing several hundred ringleaders of the mutiny, order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Zhang Xu, Military Governor of Xia-Sui-Yin, to replace him; once several hundred ringleaders of the revolt had been executed, the region was pacified.
